drafts.title: One year after the $7,500 EV credit ended: sales cooled, home charge still pays.
drafts.window: Wednesday ~11 AM MT primary; secondary ~9 PM MT. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: NPR Sep 30, 2026 (one-year mark): federal new-EV tax credit up to $7,500 ended Sep 30, 2025 under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Edmunds: EV share of new sales hit about 11.4% in Sep 2025 rush, then settled around 5-6% through 2026. Cox: EV sales down about 36% YoY late 2025 and about 27% YoY in Q1 2026 vs prior year, then more stable. Hybrids up almost 27% past year (Edmunds). Soft politics. Soft Manheim used-price tickers and lease ladders. Soft CAFE twin-only. Kitchen-table for first EV at 62: you do not need Congress to make home cents/kWh beat the pump for weekly miles. Soft-pedal "EVs are dead."
bullets: Federal new-EV credit up to $7,500 (and used-EV credit up to $4,000 in prior form) ended Sep 30, 2025; NPR marks the one-year anniversary Sep 30, 2026.
Edmunds: EV share of new U.S. sales about 11.4% in Sep 2025 (rush), then roughly 5-6% through 2026; about 5.8% in Oct 2025 after the cliff.
Cox Automotive: EV sales down about 36% YoY in late 2025 and about 27% YoY in Q1 2026 vs year-earlier periods; 2026 described as lower but stable.
Edmunds: hybrid sales up almost 27% in the past year; dealer anecdote (Massapequa Toyota): hybrid inventory turns extremely fast (about 12-day supply cited).

Cox: average EV transaction price over $54,000 in August vs just under $50,000 for gas vehicles; more than 300,000 vehicles expected off lease in the next year (used market growing; soft-pedal price ladders).
drafts.body:
One year ago today the big federal EV tax credit went away.

NPR walked the numbers this morning. Buyers rushed in September 2025. Sales cooled after. New EVs have been hanging around five to six percent of U.S. new-car sales through 2026, not the cliff some people predicted. Hybrids had a bigger year. Soft-pedal the cable-news fight. Soft-pedal party labels. Soft-pedal Manheim used-price tickers and lease ladders.

Here is the kitchen-table sticky note for a 45-year-old shopping a family EV, or a 62-year-old who already bought one after the credit died:

1) Write YOUR home cents per kilowatt-hour next to what you pay at the pump for a week of miles.
2) Soft-pedal "EVs are cancelled." Soft-pedal "gas is cancelled." Compare YOUR driveway math.
3) Soft-pedal waiting for Congress to make the monthly payment feel better. Home charge is still the independence lever.
4) If you are shopping used, ask about off-lease inventory without turning into a price-ticker account.
5) If you already drive electric, keep the cheap miles at home and use retail DC for trips.

35-54 line: Premium saves "one year after $7,500 / 5-6% share / still do home $/kWh math."

55+ line: independence is knowing your own fuel math when Washington changes the rulebook.

Before I leave Grand Junction on I-70, I screenshot the home-base charger.

As of a Sep 29 Tesla/DCFC Tracker pull, the Patterson Road Supercharger at Village Fair showed about eight stalls up to 325 kilowatts. Membership sat near $0.38 a kilowatt-hour. Public sat near $0.51. Soft-pedal turning every mountain stop into a price war post. Soft-pedal Fruita and Gypsum as twins. Soft-pedal yesterday's Vail Valley number as the only story.

Sticky notes for a 42-year-old road-tripping with kids, or a 62-year-old who got the first EV later in life:

1) Open the Tesla app or PlugShare before you leave town. Screenshot stalls and $/kWh.
2) Write home-base next to mountain-stop. Prices move. Your screenshot is the receipt.
3) Soft-pedal "charging is free." Soft-pedal "charging is impossible."
4) If you are not a Tesla, confirm NACS/CCS access at that exact site before you count on it.
5) End with a question: what is YOUR home-base public rate this week?

drafts.title: GM / Ultium: $1B to make cheaper long-range truck batteries in Tennessee by 2028.
drafts.window: Wednesday ~11 AM MT primary; secondary ~9 PM MT. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: Sep 29, 2026: Ultium Cells (GM + LG Energy Solution JV) will invest $1 billion to retool Spring Hill, Tennessee for mass production of prismatic lithium manganese-rich (LMR) cells. GM/TNECD: first in the world to mass-produce prismatic LMR; energy density about 33% greater than LFP at comparable cost; aimed at future electric trucks and full-size SUVs with over 400 miles of range; first vehicles with LMR expected 2028; upgrades begin later 2026; about 500 new jobs on top of about 1,200 current workers. Soft-pedal GM+PG&E LIVE twin. Soft-pedal lease ladders. Kitchen-table: affordable long-range trucks/SUVs are a manufacturing story with a calendar, not a same-week lease deal.
bullets: Ultium Cells announced Sep 29, 2026 plans to produce LMR prismatic cells at Spring Hill, TN; TNECD: $1 billion investment to retool/diversify the plant.
LMR designed for about 33% higher energy density than LFP at comparable cost (GM / Ultium / TNECD).
Facility upgrades begin later 2026; completion expected 2028; about 500 new jobs projected; GM cites about 1,200 current employees at the site before the add.
GM intends LMR for upcoming electric trucks and full-size SUVs aiming for over 400 miles of range; high-nickel remains the highest-range chemistry in the portfolio (Kurt Kelty).
Electrek: current longest-range Chevy Silverado EV cited up to about 478 miles on high-nickel; starts around $55,895 (sticker context, not a lease ladder).
drafts.body:
Cheaper long-range electric trucks are a factory story with a date on it.

Yesterday Ultium Cells said it will put another $1 billion into Spring Hill, Tennessee to mass-produce a new manganese-rich battery cell. The pitch is simple: about 33 percent more energy density than today's cheap LFP chemistry, at a similar cost. Tennessee officials say the plant is expected to be first in the world to mass-produce that prismatic LMR cell. Upgrades start later this year. Finish target is 2028. About 500 more jobs on a site that already employs about 1,200.

Soft-pedal lease payment ladders. Soft-pedal GM Smart Charge Bundle LIVE twin. Soft-pedal "buy this truck tomorrow." The sticky note is the calendar.

Sticky notes for a 48-year-old who needs a work truck, or a 60-year-old watching whether EVs get affordable without a luxury badge:

1) Write "2028" next to "cheaper long-range truck packs."
2) Soft-pedal waiting for one press release to drop your payment overnight.
3) Ask dealers later which chemistry is in the truck, not just the sticker.
4) Soft-pedal Manheim used-price tickers.
5) If you already drive electric, this is about the next wave of family trucks, not your current home-charge math.

35-54 line: Premium saves "$1B Spring Hill / 33% denser than LFP / 2028 trucks."

55+ line: American factory jobs plus affordable range is kitchen-table independence.

drafts.title: Fake "MyChart Medicare Kit" texts: 41 health systems warned; open enrollment starts Oct 15.
drafts.window: Wednesday ~11 AM MT primary; secondary ~9 PM MT. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: Content-shift AI/scam pocketbook for older households. Association of Health Care Journalists Sep 16, 2026 + Becker's: about 41 health systems warned patients about phishing that uses MyChart branding to push a fake free "Medicare Kit" / senior wellness package. Messages send people to fake sites to steal logins and personal/financial info. Epic/MyChart: MyChart does not hold giveaways; countdown clocks are a red flag. Medicare open enrollment begins Oct 15 (Money / AHCJ). Soft-pedal twinning overnight LIVE about AI assistants for doctor appointments - this is the scam/money frame. Kitchen-table: delete, do not click, open the real app yourself.
bullets: About 41 U.S. health systems warned patients about MyChart-branded phishing offering a free Medicare / senior wellness kit (Becker's / AHCJ Sep 2026).
Sample lure language cites limited zip-code inventory and 48-hour expiry pressure (AHCJ summarizing Gizmodo sample).
Epic reminder: MyChart does not hold giveaways; do not click links; do not pay or submit personal info; countdown clocks are a scam tell (mychart.org scam help).
Medicare open enrollment begins Oct 15 (through Dec 7 in standard season coverage cited by Money/AHCJ).
Official path: open MyChart via the real app/site; for Medicare questions use 1-800-MEDICARE; AARP Fraud Watch Network Helpline 1-877-908-3990 cited by AHCJ.
drafts.body:
AI makes fake texts look polite. Your money still needs a boring habit.

Dozens of health systems - about 41 in the recent roundup - have warned patients about fake MyChart messages pushing a free "Medicare Kit." They want your login and your wallet. Soft-pedal yesterday's AI-appointments post as a twin. Soft-pedal tech-bro takes. This is kitchen-table fraud season before Medicare open enrollment starts October 15.

Sticky notes for a 55-year-old helping parents, or a 70-year-old who uses MyChart for real lab results:

1) Delete the text or email. Do not click. Do not hit unsubscribe on a stranger link.
2) Open MyChart yourself through the real app or the bookmark you already trust.
3) Soft-pedal "free kit" pressure and countdown clocks.
4) Medicare will not cold-call you for your number to unlock a gift.
5) If you typed a card number, call the bank the same day.

35-54 line: Premium saves "fake MyChart Medicare Kit / 41 systems / Oct 15 season."

55+ line: independence is protecting the checking account before open enrollment noise hits.

drafts.window: Wednesday ~11 AM MT primary; secondary ~9 PM MT. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: Content-shift kitchen-table Powerwall decision (not a VPP map). Home Energy Decisions (updated Sep 11, 2026): honest all-in installed Powerwall 3 often about $13,000-$16,500 for one unit after the residential federal credit ended for systems placed in service after Dec 31, 2025. The Cool Down Sep 24, 2026: Louisiana homeowner quoted $24,000 to add a Powerwall 3 to an existing Powerwall 2; Reddit replies called it roughly $8,000-$10,000 high even vs California prices. Soft-pedal battery-heavy VPP. Soft-pedal Powerwall 2+3 software LIVE twin as the only post. Soft-pedal Enphase Meter Collar leftover as twin. Kitchen-table: get 2-3 itemized bids; confirm compatibility in writing. Brian is still weighing Powerwall vs Enphase storage.
bullets: Section 25D residential clean-energy credit generally not available for expenditures after Dec 31, 2025 (IRS timing; Home Energy Decisions and multiple 2026 explainers).
Home Energy Decisions: single Powerwall 3 all-in often about $13,000-$16,500 (battery, Gateway, labor, permits) in 2026 market references.
Powerwall 3 usable energy about 13.5 kWh (Tesla datasheet family cited across explainers).
The Cool Down Sep 24, 2026: Louisiana homeowner quoted $24,000 to add PW3 to existing PW2; top replies called it thousands high vs typical California pricing.
Tesla has published backward-compatibility training/limits for mixing generations; confirm with installer in writing (Cool Down / Tesla compatibility notes). Soft-pedal VPP payout maps.
drafts.body:
I am still weighing a home battery. The first filter is the quote, not the brochure.

In 2026 the big federal residential credit for a new home battery is generally gone if the system was not placed in service by the end of 2025. Market explainers put a straightforward single Powerwall 3 install somewhere around $13,000 to $16,500 all-in. Then a Louisiana homeowner posted a $24,000 quote just to add a Powerwall 3 onto a Powerwall 2. Replies called that highway robbery.

Soft-pedal VPP bounty maps. Soft-pedal "the battery pays for itself next summer." Soft-pedal software-mix LIVE as the only story.

Sticky notes for a 55-year-old with rooftop solar, or anyone shopping backup for outages:

1) Get at least two itemized bids: hardware, gateway, labor, permits, panel work.
2) Ask in writing whether PW3 + existing PW2 is supported at YOUR site.
3) Soft-pedal one scary quote. Soft-pedal one magical lowball.
4) Separate backup value from bill-savings claims.
5) Write the all-in cash number first. Financing monthly payments can hide the real total.

35-54 line: Premium saves "$13k-$16.5k ballpark / $24k red flag / itemize it."

55+ line: independence is not overpaying because you were scared of the next outage.
